-All seven CIVO-positive seeds cross the $\nve > 1.5\times$ threshold (Table~\ref{tab:post_civo}), yet the downstream damage is stochastic.\footnote{Exp\_009e was excluded from multi-seed analyses due to a seed configuration error (default seed=0, identical to exp\_008d).}  Full collapse is the majority outcome (5/7 seeds), with two self-correction cases (Walker seeds 2 and 5). Cheetah seeds exhibit more extreme overestimation (peak NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$ vs.\ Walker's $1.53$--$4.62\times$), consistent with the Cheetah reward scale amplifying the fidelity gap.  We hypothesize that the divergence relates to the critic's representational capacity at the time of CIVO onset.  \citet{lyle2022capacity} demonstrate that deep RL networks suffer progressive capacity loss, in which early-learned features become increasingly difficult to overwrite.  If the critic's capacity is already partially consumed when CIVO injects overestimation, the network cannot recalibrate (seed~0); if sufficient capacity remains, the critic can absorb transient overestimation and recover (seed~2).

\paragraph{A fourth trajectory: CIVO-induced persistent value collapse.}

Obs-decoder SGS seed~3 (exp\_025) exhibits a trajectory not observed in the untreated seeds: healthy through 105K ($
ve < 1.0	imes$, eval 818.6), CIVO onset at 135K ($
ve = 5.47	imes$, eval 67.0), followed by evaluation recovery (590.2 at 215K, 64\% of baseline) but persistent value collapse ($
ve = 0.14	imes$, value mean 80.6). The critic undershoots after the CIVO episode, suggesting that CIVO-induced representational damage may be irreversible even when the policy partially recovers. This contrasts with transient CIVO (seed~2, 009b), where both value and evaluation recover jointly, and with full collapse (seed~1, 008d), where neither recovers. Seed~4 exhibits the same terminal value collapse ($
ve = 0.14	imes$ at 215K, eval 242), suggesting this overcorrection is systematic rather than seed-specific. The pattern adds a fourth post-CIVO outcome---policy recovery with critic damage---to the three documented in Table~ef{tab:post_civo}.
